items.title: The derived limit of the quasi-coherent approximations lies in bounded above quasi-coherent complexes
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'

items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the existence-of-hulls setup, the lemma states that the derived limit K = R-lim K_n = DQ_X(R-lim K_n) of the tower of pseudo-coherent complexes belongs to D^-_QCoh(O_X) (statement lines 8405-8413). The proof has three separate moves: the coherator DQ_X exists for a quasi-compact quasi-separated X and, being a right adjoint, commutes with products and hence with derived limits, which gives the displayed equality; since DQ_X has bounded cohomological dimension it suffices to show R-lim K_n lies in D^-(O_X); and finally one takes an affine open U and uses the exact sequence relating R^1-lim H^{m-1}(U, K_n) and lim H^m(U, K_n) to H^m(U, R-lim K_n), together with the comparison of the cohomology of a pseudo-coherent complex with the cohomology of its cohomology sheaves, to reduce to the boundedness statement (proof lines 8416-8443). That boundedness is proved by a Nakayama argument along the thickening tower: with a_n the largest degree in which H^{a_n}(K_n) is nonzero, the sequence a_1 <= a_2 <= ... is shown to be constant because H^{a_n}(K_{n-1}) = H^{a_n}(K_n) tensor O_{X_{n-1}} and the module H^{a_n}(K_n) is of finite presentation, so vanishing after the thickening forces vanishing (proof lines 8446-8458). The reduction to a boundedness statement and the Nakayama step are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
